title: Standardized protocol for determination of biohydrogen potential
author: Carrillo-Reyes, Buitrón, et al.
materials: AMPTS II system incubation and monitoring1Fill the incubation unit with distilled water and set to a temperature of 37 °C.2Connect the agitation systems of each bottle serially with the motor cables, and the first motor to the Motor Controller.3Connect the 12 V power adapter to the Gas Volume Measuring Device, and to a 100−240 V 50/60 Hz standard power socket. After this, connect the 24 V power adapter to the Motor Controller and to a 100−240 V 50/60 Hz standard power socket.4Set the System switch on the Motor Controller to ON, and set the ON/OFF switches on each motor unit to ON.5Empty each flow cell in the gas volume measuring device.6Adjust the motor speed to 60 % (approx. 120 rpm), with intermittent mixing at 60 s ON and 180 s OFF. Activate the motor setting the control to ON and apply the settings.7Start the data logging program according to the AMPTS II software manual.8Analyze the gas composition to determine the hydrogen fraction in the biogas samples, for each bottle at least once during the kinetics. Disconnect the Tygon® hose from the absorber unit and seal it with a pipe plug and take the biogas sample with a syringe from the other hose.9Check daily that the hard tubing pieces that connect the bent stir rod to the motor are undamaged and the mixing works properly. Otherwise, change the tubing pieces.10Check daily that the water level in the thermostatic water bath reaches the plastic lid and fill it with additional distilled water if necessary. Make sure that the Tygon® hose is not bent abruptly, interfering with the gas flow and not being damaged by the rotating parts of the agitator/motor.11Verify that the water level in the gas volume measurement device is within the recommended range. Fill with additional deionized or distilled water to the recommended water level when necessary.12The thymolphthalein pH indicator in solution F will change from blue to colorless when the CO2 absorption capacity of the NaOH solution drops below the optimum. At this point, it is recommended to replace the bottle with new solution F to prevent the CO2 gas from passing to the gas volume measuring device. Approximately 2.9 L of CO2 can be captured (at 22 °C) in each bottle before it needs to be changed.13To change the solution F, place pipe plugs on the hoses of the incubation unit and gas measuring device. Replace the old solution with a new one, reconnect the hoses and remove the pipe plugs.

End of the test1The AMPTS II software automatically upgrades the cumulative hydrogen production curve; review the curve daily to determine the end of the essay following the stop criteria. The stop time criterion (ST) is obtained when the H2 production curve becomes asymptotic (FT) (Fig. 4) [8]. As an additional stop criterion, you can use the coefficient of variation between the last three records of cumulative hydrogen when it becomes lower than 5 %.2In the AMPTS II software, generate a report in the Download report menu. Download the report and open it to make sure that the report has been generated correctly and that no errors have occurred during the download of the file.3Stop the registration by pressing the pause button and then the stop button. Note: By pressing the stop button, the experiment associated with that particular cell can no longer continue.4Turn off the thermostatic water bath.5Set the on/off switch of each motor unit to OFF.6Set the system switch on the motor controller to OFF.7Unplug the power adapters (for the motor controller and the gas volume measuring device) from the power supply.8Disconnect the hoses between the reactors and the NaOH bottles.9Disconnect the hoses between the NaOH bottles and the gas volume measuring device.10Empty the water bath using the manual water pump included with the equipment.

steps.title: Prepare inoculum
steps.instruction: Thermally pretreat sludge from an anaerobic wastewater treatment reactor at 105 °C for 24 h, cool, grind, sieve to particles <850 μm, and determine volatile solids (VS) content by standard methods.

steps.title: Label manual serum bottles
steps.instruction: Label all serum bottles; include triplicates for each condition and triplicate endogenous controls (no substrate).

steps.title: Add inoculum for manual test
steps.instruction: Calculate inoculum to obtain an S/X ratio of 2.7 (g substrate · g VS⁻¹) for a working volume of 80 mL and an initial carbohydrate concentration of 5 g L⁻¹; weigh the exact amount directly into each serum bottle.

steps.title: Add solution A
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of solution A to each bottle using a graduated or air‑displacement pipette.

steps.title: Add solution B (substrate)
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL of solution B to each bottle (except endogenous controls) to give an initial glucose concentration of 5 g L⁻¹.

steps.title: Add distilled water
steps.instruction: Add distilled water to bring the total volume to 80 mL: 71 mL for bottles containing solution B and 75 mL for endogenous controls; this leaves a headspace of 40 mL.

steps.title: Adjust initial pH
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH to 7.5 by adding drops of solution C or D with a Pasteur pipette as needed.

steps.title: Seal bottles
steps.instruction: Close each bottle with a rubber stopper and secure it with an aluminum ring using a crimper.

steps.title: Perform headspace N₂ flush
steps.instruction: Insert a needle connected to a hose into the bottle, flush the headspace with N₂ for 30 s while a second needle allows gas to escape; remove both needles simultaneously after flushing.

steps.title: Start incubation
steps.instruction: Begin incubation close to noon (12:00 h) at 37 °C with orbital shaking at 150 rpm.

steps.title: Release pressure after 1 h
steps.instruction: After one hour of incubation, discharge excess pressure from each bottle into the water‑filled inverted graduated cylinder.

steps.title: Measure biogas volume
steps.instruction: Every 3–4 h, record the displaced water volume and the temperature of the acid water in the inverted cylinder.

steps.title: Sample gas for composition
steps.instruction: Before each gas sample, purge the hose; analyze H₂ and CO₂ by gas chromatography at least once per day.

steps.title: Determine end of test
steps.instruction: Stop the test when the cumulative H₂ production curve becomes asymptotic (final time, FT) or when the coefficient of variation of the last three cumulative H₂ records falls below 5 %.

steps.title: Remove bottles after test
steps.instruction: Take the serum bottles out of the incubator; proceed to the sampling and analysis steps described later.

steps.title: Prepare acid water for cylinder
steps.instruction: Acidify 500 mL of distilled water with 10 mL of solution C (pH < 2) to prevent CO₂ dissolution.

steps.title: Fill inverted graduated cylinder
steps.instruction: Using a hose, syringe, and three‑way stopcock, fill a 100 mL inverted graduated cylinder with the acid water.

steps.title: Measure biogas displacement
steps.instruction: Close the stopcock, insert a needle through the serum bottle stopper, open the stopcock so biogas displaces the water, and record the displaced volume.

steps.title: Collect biogas sample
steps.instruction: Take the biogas sample either from the displaced water in the cylinder or directly from the serum bottle with a chromatography syringe.

steps.title: Label automatic AMPTS II bottles
steps.instruction: Label all Schott bottles; include triplicates for each condition and triplicate endogenous controls (or blanks).

steps.title: Prepare CO₂ absorption unit
steps.instruction: Add 80 mL of solution F to each CO₂ absorption bottle, place a plastic stopper with two tubing ports.

steps.title: Connect biogas hoses
steps.instruction: Connect the biogas hoses from each CO₂ absorption bottle to the corresponding bottle in the incubation unit according to the AMPTS II manual.

steps.title: Add inoculum for automatic test
steps.instruction: Calculate inoculum to keep an S/X ratio of 2.7 for a working volume of 360 mL and 5 g L⁻¹ carbohydrate; weigh the inoculum in a glass beaker.

steps.title: Add solution A (automatic)
steps.instruction: Add 22.6 mL of solution A to each glass bottle using a graduated or air‑displacement pipette.

steps.title: Add solution B (automatic)
steps.instruction: Add 36 mL of solution B to each bottle (except endogenous controls) to obtain an initial glucose concentration of 5 g L⁻¹.

steps.title: Add inoculum and suspend sludge
steps.instruction: Add the weighed inoculum to each bottle; suspend any remaining sludge in the beaker with water and add this suspension to the corresponding bottle.

steps.title: Add distilled water (automatic)
steps.instruction: Complete the 360 mL working volume by adding distilled water: 301.4 mL for substrate bottles and 337.4 mL for endogenous controls; headspace will be 240 mL (V/W ratio = 1.5).

steps.title: Adjust pH (automatic)
steps.instruction: Adjust the initial pH to 7.5 by adding drops of solution C or D with a Pasteur pipette.

steps.title: Apply stopcock grease
steps.instruction: Apply a thin layer of stopcock grease to the bottle thread and the external opening to avoid gas leaks.

steps.title: Install bottle stoppers and motor
steps.instruction: Place the bottle stoppers with two tubing ports and rotating shaft, attach the multifunction brushless DC motor, and connect a Tygon® hose to the ports.

steps.title: Connect hoses to absorption unit
steps.instruction: Connect one hose to the corresponding CO₂ absorption bottle and seal the other hose with a pipe plug.

steps.title: Headspace exchange (automatic)
steps.instruction: Temporarily disconnect the Tygon® hose, vent excess pressure into a water beaker, attach N₂ flow and flush the headspace for 30 s, then reseal the hose with the pipe plug and reconnect.

steps.title: Set up incubation water bath
steps.instruction: Fill the incubation unit with distilled water and set the temperature to 37 °C.

steps.title: Connect agitation system
steps.instruction: Serially connect the agitation cables of each bottle to the motor controller and attach the 12 V adapter to the gas‑volume measuring device and the 24 V adapter to the motor controller; plug both into a 100‑240 V 50/60 Hz mains socket.

steps.title: Power on motors
steps.instruction: Turn the system switch on the motor controller to ON and set each motor unit ON/OFF switch to ON.

steps.title: Prepare gas‑volume device
steps.instruction: Empty each flow cell in the gas‑volume measuring device.

steps.title: Set motor mixing program
steps.instruction: Set motor speed to 60 % (≈120 rpm) with intermittent mixing: 60 s ON, 180 s OFF; activate the motor.

steps.title: Start data logging
steps.instruction: Launch the AMPTS II data‑logging program according to the software manual.

steps.title: Analyze gas composition
steps.instruction: At least once during the kinetics, determine the hydrogen fraction in the biogas; disconnect the Tygon® hose from the absorber, seal it, and draw a sample with a syringe from the other hose.

steps.title: Daily equipment checks
steps.instruction: Inspect mixing tubing for damage and replace if needed; verify water level in the thermostatic bath reaches the lid and add water if necessary; ensure the Tygon® hose is not sharply bent; confirm water level in the gas‑volume device is within range and add water if low.

steps.title: Monitor CO₂ absorption capacity
steps.instruction: Observe the thymolphthalein indicator in solution F (blue → colorless); when it turns colorless, replace solution F because ≈2.9 L CO₂ (22 °C) has been captured per bottle.

steps.title: Replace solution F
steps.instruction: Place pipe plugs on both hoses, replace the old solution F with fresh solution, reconnect the hoses, and remove the plugs.

steps.title: Determine end of automatic test
steps.instruction: Review the cumulative hydrogen curve daily; stop when the curve becomes asymptotic or when the CV of the last three cumulative H₂ records falls below 5 %.

steps.title: Generate and download report
steps.instruction: In the AMPTS II software, generate a report via the Download Report menu, download it, and verify that it contains no errors.

steps.title: Stop registration and power down
steps.instruction: Press the pause button then the stop button (experiment cannot continue after stop); turn off the thermostatic water bath, switch each motor unit OFF, switch the motor‑controller OFF, and unplug all power adapters.

steps.title: Disconnect hoses and empty bath
steps.instruction: Disconnect hoses between reactors and NaOH bottles, then between NaOH bottles and the gas‑volume measuring device; empty the water bath using the manual pump.

steps.title: Open bottles and record pH
steps.instruction: After the kinetic phase, open each bottle and record the liquid pH.

steps.title: Determine suspended solids
steps.instruction: Keep bottles under magnetic stirring; take a homogeneous 20 mL sample and determine total and volatile suspended solids in duplicate (5 mL per duplicate) according to standard methods.

steps.title: Prepare samples for COD and metabolites
steps.instruction: Take another 20 mL sample, acidify with concentrated H₂SO₄ to pH < 2, then centrifuge at 3600 rpm for 10 min (or higher).

steps.title: Filter supernatant
steps.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 μm nitrocellulose filter (use a 1.5 μm glass‑fiber filter first if many solids are present); store filtrate at 4 °C for no more than 7 days.

steps.title: Analyze COD and metabolites
steps.instruction: Analyze COD by standard methods, fermentation products by gas or liquid chromatography, and residual carbohydrates by the phenol‑sulfuric acid method.

steps.title: Validate COD and carbohydrate methods
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 g anhydrous glucose (dried at 105 °C for 2 h and stored in a desiccator), dilute to 1 L with distilled water, and analyze COD and carbohydrates; theoretical COD of glucose is 1.067 g COD g⁻¹ glucose. If results differ, review the analytical procedure and calibration curves.

steps.title: Validate fermentation product analysis
steps.instruction: Use certified reference materials (e.g., Volatile Free Acid Mix CRM46975‑Supelco and Lactic Acid PHR1215‑Supelco) to validate the measurement of fermentation products.

description: The present method was validated in 8 independent laboratories from 5 different countries (Brazil, Chile, France, Mexico and Uruguay); a detailed discussion about its development, validation and consideration of workload time were already published [4]. Average values of cumulative hydrogen production (Hmax) and the corresponding standard deviations were used to calculate the intra-laboratory and inter-laboratory coefficient of variation (CV) as repeatability and reproducibility indicators, respectively. Applying the present protocol, the average intra-laboratory coefficient of variation ranged from 13 % to 9 % using the manual and the automatic protocol, respectively. But using the automatic protocol, the interlaboratory variation could be reduced up to 15 % with the HTT as inoculum; which is an acceptable result according to studies analyzing the biochemical methane potential (Fig. 7) [13].Fig. 7Cumulative hydrogen production (Hmax) specific to the working volume (L H2 L−1), for the manual and automatic protocols, and its corresponding intra- and inter-laboratory variation. For the manual protocol evaluation different inoculum were tested by different laboratories, meanwhile for the automatic protocol three different source of inoculum were evaluated in different laboratories. The different inoculum sources were heat-treated anaerobic sludge from a thermophilic digester (HTT); heat-treated anaerobic sludge from a mesophilic digester (HTM); biomass from an auto-fermented effluent rich in sucrose (AF); aerobic sludge pretreated by cell wash-out (WO); compost from kitchen wastes (C); and heat-treated anaerobic sludge from a digester treating solid wastes (HTS). L1–L8 stands for results from different laboratories.Fig. 7
